newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end down, focus on power prices.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end down, focus on power prices.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed marginally lower in erratic trade with investors worried about how far the government will cut generating prices in its review next month, said dealers.
The bolsa may open slightly higher with attention remaining focused in the electricity sector, they said.
The selective IPSA index closed down 0.09 percent at 101.37 points. The general IGPA index shed 0.07 percent to 5,511.38 points in volume of 12.2 billion pesos.
Traders said the light volume reflected the reticence of institutional investors to enter the market with any force.

Electricity shares closed broadly lower on fears about the impact of the price review with investors selling power stocks to take positions in industrial companies and cellulose producers, said traders.
"The electricity sector is being punished by jitters over how far generating prices could drop," said one dealer.

Analysts have said generating prices could drop by around eight percent to take into account lower operating costs as the result of the building of a natural gas pipeline from Argentina, which will be completed next year.
The prices will be in force for the next six months.
Endesa lost 0.28 percent to 263-1/2 pesos, while Chilgener shed 0.20 percent to 2,470 pesos.
Winners included telecoms company Entel, up 0.65 percent at 3,875 pesos, winery Concha y Toro, up 0.61 percent at 166 pesos and pulp producer Copec which rose 0.28 percent to 1,815 pesos.
